standard_prerequisites.name: The complementary idempotent
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that for an idempotent f the endomorphism g = id - f satisfies f g = g f = 0 and g g = g, so the statement may be applied with the roles of f and g exchanged.

standard_prerequisites.name: A kernel map is a monomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the kernel map i can be cancelled on the left, which turns the identity i p i = i into p i = id.

core_obligations: Part (1), the splitting (proof lines 612-616): the computation i = (f + g) i = g i together with the defining property of p gives i p i = i, and cancelling i on the left yields p i = id.

Part (1), the universal property of the cokernel (proof lines 618-628): given a : x -> y with a f = 0 the author computes a = a (f + g) = a g = a i p, which exhibits a as b p with b = a i, and uniqueness follows from b = b p i = a i, so p is the cokernel of f.
Parts (2), (3) and (4) (proof lines 630-635): they follow by duality and by the symmetry of the situation, since g is again idempotent.
proof_roadmap: Use the complementary idempotent to identify the given kernel map with a composite through g.
Cancel the kernel map to get the section and prove the universal property of the cokernel.
Dualize and exchange the roles of f and g for the remaining assertions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the kernel and the cokernel of an idempotent endomorphism of an object of a preadditive category: each of the two, when it exists, is split by a morphism built from the complementary idempotent and serves as the other (statement lines 583-609). The proof is a complete argument for the first assertion, giving both the splitting of the kernel map and the universal property of the cokernel by explicit computations with the complementary idempotent (proof lines 612-628), after which the remaining assertions follow by duality and by exchanging the roles of the two idempotents (proof lines 630-635). The non-formal content is the construction of the splitting and of the map witnessing the universal property. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
